title: Immunologic characterization of platelet-rich plasma (PRP) to identify biomarkers as predictors of response when used in osteoarthrosis patients
summary:
The number of patients suffering from osteoarthritis or tendinopathy continuously grows. In addition to regular conservative and operative therapy strategies, regenerative therapies gained interests of patients and practitioners. With these, pain may be sufficiently reduced and joint function may be preserved.
In regenerative therapies (also known as “orthobiologics”) endogenous substances and cells are used. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) is leading the field of osteoarthritis and tendinopathy therapy. A small blood sample needs to be centrifuged to obtain the supernatant. This plasma product contains high concentrations of immunoactive cells which may help endogenous regeneration. Practitioners may use this product to inject it into affected joints, or in or around affected tendons.
Thus far, the definite mechanism of action is not fully clarified. However, up to 70 % of patients report a reduction of previous symptoms following PRP therapy. We hypothesize that this may be a result of patient’s individual immune system. Different levels of immunoactive cells may interfere with such regenerative therapies.

Therefore, we aim to monitor PRP patients in our outpatient clinic including regular examinations, lab tests. and immunologic assessments for a time period of 6 months following PRP therapy.

interventions.name: We aim to include a total of 120 patients from the outpatient clinic of the CMSC with a symptomatic osteoarthritis of the shoulder, the hip, or the knee or with a symptomatic tendinopathy of the supraspinatus, biceps, patellar, or achilles tendon. Twenty patients per disease group shall be included.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Volljährige Patient*innen jeden Geschlechts, 
Symptomatische Gonarthrose des Hauptbelastungsbeins (Arthrosegrad I - III nach Kellgren-Lawrence bzw. OARSI-Joint Space Narrowing Score I - II),
Symptomatische Coxarthrose (Arthrosegrad I - II nach Kellgren-Lawrence),
Symptomatische Omarthrose (Arthrosegrad I - II nach Kellgren-Lawrence),
Symptomatische Tendinopathien (Achillessehne, Bicepssehne, Patellasehne) 

age > 17 years, osteoarthritis of the knee (Kellgren-Lawrence I - II), osteoarthritis of the hip (Kellgren-Lawrence I - II), osteoarthritis of the shoulder (Kellgren-Lawrence I - II), symptomatic tendinopathy (achilles tendon, biceps tendon, patellar tendon)
Exclusion criteria:
General exclusion criteria: no consent in study participation, inflammatory/rheumatic disease; exclusion criteria for osteoarthritis patients: major trauma or surgery at the affected joint within the past 12 months, arthroscopy of the affected joint within the past 12 months, previous procedure at the cartilage of the affected joint within the past 12 months, previous injection therapy within the past 12 months; exclusion criteria for tendinopathy patients: surgery at the affected tendon within the past 12 months, previous injection therapy within the past 12 months
